chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Khalid ibn Jarir, from Abu Al-Rabie Al-Shamy, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) disliked bartering one Qafeez of almonds for two Qafeez of almonds, and one Qafeez of dates for two Qafeez of dates.

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah, a title for Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him).
key_terms.قَفِيز: A traditional unit of volume measurement used for dry goods like grains and dates.
key_terms.كَرِهَ: Disliked (indicating a preferred avoidance or mild prohibition in fiqh).

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) say about exchanging unequal quantities of the same food item?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) disliked exchanging a qafiz of almonds or dates for two qafiz of the same, a ruling that underscores the principle of 'fadl' (excess) in barter to prevent hidden usury (riba al-fadl). This specific narration from al-Kafi highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on precise measurement and equality in spot transactions of identical commodities to ensure justice in trade.
